content.readme:
net-merge

Use all your internet connections at the same time.
Combine Wi-Fi, Ethernet and phone hotspots, so downloads, games and browsers get the speed of every connection added up.

Website · Download · Android · Install · Add a second connection · Troubleshooting · How it works

From the same developer: DormHost, put your college project online. Node.js, Python or Docker with a database, 30 days free.

Need more control? Try RoutEngine, the upgraded commercial version of net-merge.
Choose the connection for each app, add a fallback, and set a speed limit or data cap per app. Windows, macOS and Linux. Free for personal use, Pro for work.


A Mac with Wi-Fi + an Android phone. The menu shows both connections working at once. Watch the full 45-second video.

net-merge uses all your network adapters together. It works on **Windows, macOS and Linux**. It is free. There is no account, no server and no VPN. A real test with Wi-Fi + an Android USB tether + an iPhone hotspot, 9 downloads at once: **232-303 Mbit/s**. The fastest connection alone gave about 121 Mbit/s. | Windows: hover the icon | Windows: the menu | macOS: the menu bar | |---|---|---| | ![Tooltip: Merging, speed of each adapter and the total](docs/tray-tooltip.png) | ![Menu: total, each adapter's speed and flows, IPv6 option, Pause merging, Quit](docs/tray-menu.png) | ![macOS menu: total 399 Mbit/s, en0 and feth0 each with their flows, Pause merging, Quit](docs/tray-menu-macos.png) | ## How it helps net-merge gives every new connection to one of your links. When an app opens many connections, they spread over all your links. - **Good for:** Steam and game downloads, browsers, system updates, cloud uploads (Google Drive), download managers like IDM, torrents. - **Not for:** one single connection. One connection always uses one link, so one big file from one connection does not get faster. Browsers can split a download into several connections; see the tip under [Use it](#use-it). - **Works for every app**, TCP and UDP, IPv4 and IPv6. You do not set up a proxy. - **Smart:** faster links get more connections. A link with no internet gets none until it works again. - **Safe:** if net-merge crashes, you

# ARTEX — Global Edition **An autonomous penetration-testing system driven by LLM multi-agents** (Go backend + Next.js frontend) The UI and generated output default to English, and **can be switched to Korean, Chinese, Spanish or Japanese in Settings (System → Settings → Display language).** Changing the language also changes the language of agent-generated reports, summaries and chat replies. English · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [中文](README.zh.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) [![ci](https://github.com/jiwoochris/artex-global/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/jiwoochris/artex-global/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![detections](https://github.com/jiwoochris/artex-global/actions/workflows/detections.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/jiwoochris/artex-global/actions/workflows/detections.yml) [![web](https://github.com/jiwoochris/artex-global/actions/workflows/web.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/jiwoochris/artex-global/actions/workflows/web.yml) [![license: AGPL-3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
--- > ## 🚨 Security & misuse warning — read this first > > **This repository is published for use only within authorized environments, and only to build defensive and detection capabilities.** > > ARTEX is an autonomous offensive tool powerful enough to carry an attack from reconnaissance through intrusion to data exfiltration with little human involvement, so the harm from misuse is correspondingly large. In October 2026, several Korean news outlets reported that investigators had found indications the upstream ARTEX was used in personal-data breaches targeting Korean financial institutions; the related investigation is ongoing. This global edition is not published to help attackers. Its purpose is to help defenders understand how such autonomous AI attacks work and build the capability to detect and block them. > > - **Unauthorized use is a crime in itself.** Do not run any scanning, probing, or exploitation against systems you do not own or for which you lack explicit written authorization. In the Republic of Korea, unauthorized intrusion into an information and communications network violates the Network Act, and the Personal Information Protection Act also applies where personal data is involved. > - **Do not target live services or other parties' assets.** Verify only in learning, research, and locally isolated environments you own (deliberately vulnerable targets such as OWASP Juice Shop or DVWA). > - **Read it from a defender's point of view.** This repository also compiles defensive and detection material, such as detection signatures and hardening checklists, for autonomous AI attacks. → **[Defense & Detection Guide](docs/defense-en.md)** (also in [Korean](docs/defense-ko.md)) > > If you do not agree to this warning and to the [usage restrictions and disclaimer](#license-and-disclaimer) below, do not download or use this repository. --- > **This repository is a localized edition of the Chinese open-source project [Autumn-27/ARTEX](https://github.com/Autumn-27/ARTEX) (AGPL-3.0 · upstream repository currently unreachable, checked 2026-10), adapted so that users and teams worldwide can adopt it as-is.** To preserve the agents' decision-making performance, the internal reasoning prompts are kept in the original language, and only the user-facing output (findings, summaries, reports, chat replies) is forced into the selected language (English by default). See ["Why a global edition"](#why-a-global-edition) below for the rationale. ARTEX is a system in which several LLM-driven agents autonomously run a penetration test: they **break goals down on their own, execute real tools, and accumulate discovered assets and vulnerabilities into a graph** as they go. A single Go binary ships with the Next.js frontend embedded, and all data is stored in PostgreSQL. > **Note on this edition's language.** This fork makes the product usable in five languages — **English (default), Korean, Chinese, Spanish, and Japanese** — selectable in Settings. The user-facing output is forced into the selected language, while the agents' internal reasoning prompts are kept in the original language to preserve benchmarked performance. See [Configuration](#configuration) for how the output language is enforced by a small code-fixed directive. --- ## ⚠️ Read first — authorized use and legal notice ARTEX may be used **only against targets you own or for which you have explicit written authorization.** Any scanning, probing, or exploitation beyond the authorized scope may itself be illegal. - In the Republic of Korea, intruding into or disrupting another party's information and communications network without authorization violates the **Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection** (정보통신망법). - Personal data collected or exposed during a penetratio

# ARTEX AI autonomous penetration testing system. Multi-agent LLM, Go backend, Next.js frontend. AI 自主渗透测试系统（Go 后端 + Next.js 前端）。 [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/trhhubsd/ARTEX)](https://github.com/trhhubsd/ARTEX/releases) [![License: AGPL-3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blue)](LICENSE)
ARTEX is a multi-agent system for autonomous penetration testing in an isolated lab: a planner and workers share an asset graph and an exploration graph, with human-in-the-loop approval and full traffic recording. It ships as one binary or a Docker Compose stack. --- ## 截图预览 | 仪表盘（总览 / Token 消耗 / 活动流） | 任务列表 | | :---: | :---: | | ![仪表盘](screenshots/dashboard.png) | ![任务](screenshots/tasks.png) | | 任务 · 执行过程（会话 / 工具调用） | 探索链路 | | :---: | :---: | | ![执行过程](screenshots/sessions.png) | ![探索链路](screenshots/graph.png) | | 发现 | 资产 | | :---: | :---: | | ![发现](screenshots/findings.png) | ![资产](screenshots/assets.png) | | 资产覆盖图（力导向布局 · 已测高亮 · 节点折叠展开） | | :---: | | ![资产覆盖图](screenshots/assets_test.png) | | 流量录制 | 人在环路对话 | | :---: | :---: | | ![流量](screenshots/traffic.png) | ![对话](screenshots/chat.png) | | Agent 管理 | LLM 配置 | | :---: | :---: | | ![Agent](screenshots/agents.png) | ![LLM](screenshots/llm.png) | | 拦截审批 | 后端日志 | | :---: | :---: | | ![拦截](screenshots/intercept.png) | ![日志](screenshots/logs.png) | --- ## 审批记录详情 全局「审批记录」、任务内「拦截审批」及对话中的审批卡片均支持展开查看详情。展示结构参考 [AegisHook 的审批详情组件](https://github.com/RuoJi6/AegisHook/blob/main/web/src/components/CallDetail.vue)，沿用 ARTEX 的组件和主题： ## 资产同步（ScopeSentry） 支持从 [ScopeSentry](https://github.com/Autumn-27/ScopeSentry) 直接同步资产数据，免去重复收集： - 在「**资产同步**」页填 ScopeSentry 的地址与 API Key，接入数据源； - 按**项目**或**任务**维度选择要同步的目标与资产类型（域名 / 子域 / IP / 端口 / 站点 / 端点…）； - 一键导入并按公司资产范围归并，直接进入 ARTEX 的资产图供 agent 探索使用。 --- ## 安装 > 依赖数据库 **PostgreSQL**；探索需配置 **LLM**（`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` 或 `OPENAI_API_KEY`，也可在 UI 里配）。 ### 方式一：一键安装脚本（推荐） ```bash git clone https://github.com/trhhubsd/ARTEX cd ARTEX ./install.sh ``` 脚本会：检测 / 自动安装 Docker → 让你选 **① 全部 Docker** 或 **② 本地编译运行**： - **① 全部 Docker**：填一个 Postgres 密码（可回车随机）→ 自动写 `.env` → `docker compose up -d`。 - **② 本地运行**：选数据库（连已有 / 用 Docker 起一个）→ 生成 `config.json` → `go` 编译内嵌单二进制 → 启动。 装好后打开 **http://localhost:8787** （首次进入 `/setup` 设置管理员密码）。 ### 方式二：Docker Compose（推荐） ```bash git clone https://github.com/trhhubsd/ARTEX cd ARTEX cp .env.example .env # 填 POSTGRES_PASSWORD、可选 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY docker compose up -d # 拉取 tomicdd/artex 镜像 + postgres # → http://localhost:8787 ``` 镜像已含常用工具（ripgrep/curl/vim/npm/nmap…）；`./skills` 与 `./data` 以绑定挂载持久化。 远程 MCP 可在系统设置中选择 `http`（Streamable HTTP）或 `sse`（旧版 SSE）。 旧版 SSE 服务通常使用 `GET /sse` 建立事件流，再通过服务返回的 `/message?sessionId=...` 接收 JSON-RPC 请求；配置时将 URL 填为 `/sse`，请求头按 `Authorization=Bearer ` 填写。 ### 方式三：从源码编译单二进制 ```bash # 1) 前端静态导出 cd web && npm ci && npm run build:static && cd .. # 2) 拷进内嵌目录 cp -r web/out server/webui/dist # 3) 编译（-tags embedui 才内嵌前端） CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags embedui -o artex ./cmd/artex ./start.sh ``` ### 方式五：构建跨平台 Release 压缩包 `build.sh` 会先构建并嵌入前端，再使用 Go linker 去除调试信息，并将发布文件压缩为 zip。Release 模式默认生成 Linux amd64/arm64、macOS amd64/arm64 和 Windows amd64 的 zip 包： ```bash ./build.sh --release # 产物：dist/artex-0.3.3-*.zip ``` UPX 自解压二进制可能与部分 Linux 内核、虚拟化环境或安全策略不兼容，因此默认不启用。可用 `ARTEX_TARGETS` 自定义目标；确认目标运行环境兼容时，可显式传入 `--upx` 进一步缩小二进制： ```bash ARTEX_TARGETS=linux/amd64,windows/amd64 ./build.sh --release ./build.sh --target linux/amd64 --upx ``` --- ## 更新升级 > 升级只换程序、不动数据：Postgres 数据卷 `pgdata`、`./data`（jwt.key / SQLite 等）、`./skills` 都会保留。**数据库迁移无需手动执行**——`artex` 每次启动会幂等重跑 `schema.sql`（含 `ADD COLUMN` / `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`），即“重启即迁移”。升级前仍建议先备份 `./data` 与数据库。 ### 方式一：页面一键更新（推荐） 在 **系统配置** 页（侧边栏「系统配置」→ `/system/settings`）的**版本与更新**卡片里，可以直接检查并安装新版本，无需登录服务器。 点「更新」后：下载当前平台的发布包 → 比对 Release 的 `SHA256SUMS` → 用 `-h` 冒烟测试新二进制 → 暂存为 `artex.new` → 程序退出，由 `start.sh` / `start.bat` 重新拉起并完成换装。页面会自动等到新版本上线后刷新。 - **失败不会留下坏程序**：校验或冒烟不通过就丢弃暂存件、继续跑当前版本；换装后的新版若连续 3 次启动失败，会自动回滚到 `artex.old`（失败的那个留作 `artex.failed` 供排查）。 - **随时可回退**：上一版本保留为 `artex.old`，卡片上有「回滚到上一版本」。注意数据库结构不会回退。 - **更新会中断正在运行的任务**——更新即重启，请在空闲时进行。 - **开发构建不给更新**：版本号是 `dev` 或 `git describe` 带后缀时禁用，避免正式版覆盖掉本地调试的二进制。 - **Docker 下只换程序、不换镜像**：镜像里的 playwright / nmap 等工具链不会跟着升级，且 `docker compose up -d` 重建容器后会退回镜像自带的版本。要连镜像一起升级仍请用 `docker compose pull artex && docker compose up -d artex`。 - 访问 GitHub 需要代理时，在同一页面配置**全局代理**即可，更新链路会走它。更新只从 GitHub 域名下载并强制 HTTPS。 ### 方式二：一键更新脚本 ```bash cd ARTEX ./update.sh ``` 脚本先可选 `git pull` 拉取最新代码，再让你选 **① Docker 更新** 或 **② 本地编译更新**（与 `install.sh` 对应）： - **① Docker**：可指定目标镜像 tag（回车沿用 `.env` 的 `ARTEX_TAG`，缺省 `latest`）→ `docker compose pull` → `docker compose up -d`（换新镜像重启即自动迁移）。 - **② 本地**：重建前端静态产物 → 重新编译 `./artex`（完成后重启进程生效）。 ### 方式三：Docker Compose（手动） ```bash cd ARTEX git pull # 更新 compose / 脚本（可选） # 指定版本：在 .env 设 ARTEX_TAG=v0.2.0；不设则用 latest docker compose pull artex docker compose up -d artex # 换新镜像重启 → 自

content.readme:
# XGift

X (Twitter) Premium 礼品兑换平台。你生成兑换码发给用户，用户在网页上输入兑换码和自己的 X 用户名，系统自动完成 Premium 赠送的下单与付款。

- **兑换页**：用户自助兑换，实时显示处理进度
- **管理后台**：生成/停用兑换码、批次文件夹、统计面板、订单状态
- **安全**：凭据逐条 AES-256-GCM 加密存储，付款前逐项校验金额与商户，付款确认只提交一次

## 截图

以下截图来自本地模拟预览（全部为示例数据）：

| 兑换页 | 管理页（统计概览） |
|---|---|
| ![兑换页](docs/screenshots/redeem-light.png) | ![管理页 · 浅色](docs/screenshots/admin-light.png) |

管理页深色模式：

![管理页 · 深色](docs/screenshots/admin-dark.png)

## 本地预览（不写任何真实配置）

想先看看界面？只需要 Node.js 22+：

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm run preview
```

打开 http://127.0.0.1:4173 是兑换页，http://127.0.0.1:4173/admin 是管理后台。所有数据都是内存示例，不连接真实服务。在兑换页输入 `XG-` 加 48 个字母 `A` 可以演示完整成功流程。

## 部署教程

### 第一步：准备这些东西

部署前请先准备好以下四样东西，配置向导会逐项询问：

1. **X 登录 Cookie**（`auth_token` 和 `ct0`）：在浏览器登录 x.com 后，按 F12 打开开发者工具 → Application（应用）→ Cookies → `https://x.com`，复制这两项的值。这是系统以你的 X 账号身份发起赠送的凭据。
2. **用于付款的银行卡（一张或多张）**：卡号、有效期、CVC，以及发卡行登记的持卡人姓名、账单邮箱和账单国家（两位代码，如 `BD`）。多张卡会在服务端加密保存并随机轮换，新卡可复用同一账单资料。请只填真实信息。
3. **代理（可选）**：服务器能直接访问 x.com 就选「直连」；否则准备一个代理节点。支持 sing-box 的任意 outbound 类型（anytls、socks、http、shadowsocks、vmess、vless、trojan 等），也可以直接粘贴完整 sing-box 配置。
4. **Stripe 公钥**：X 结账页面使用的 `pk_live_` 开头公钥。使用默认 X Premium 目录时向导会说明；它与商户、商品、价格一起保存在「目录」配置中，也可以完全自定义。

网络路径独立配置：X 账号与资格检查始终直连；生成付款链接所需的地区报价校验与创建链接使用同一个 `proxy` 出口，避免币种和金额因地区不同而变化；X 请求不读取环境代理；Stripe 可使用包含 `direct` 的 `payment-outbounds` 节点池。连接故障触发 30 分钟冷却，安全查询最多尝试 3 个出口；付款确认不会自动重放。未配置或空数组时，新订单直连。Stripe 不读取环境代理。详见 [付款节点池配置](docs/payment-outbounds.md)。直接在浏览器打开 Stripe 链接时使用浏览器网络。

另外需要：一台 Linux 服务器、一个指向该服务器的域名、服务器上安装 Go 1.27+（或在自己电脑上构建后上传二进制）。

### 第二步：构建

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mizorewww/x_gift_bot.git
cd x_gift_bot
npm ci && npm run build        # 构建前端（只需一次，产物已随仓库提交时可跳过）
go build -tags with_quic,with_utls -o bin/xgift ./cmd/xgift
go build -tags with_quic,with_utls -o bin/xgift-web ./cmd/xgift-web
```

### 第三步：运行配置向导

```sh
./bin/xgift setup
```

向导会一步步引导你完成配置，全程有中文提示：

1. **密码文件** — 自动生成一个随机密码用于加密保管库，保存在你指定的路径（默认 `sqlite/vault-password`，仅本人可读）。**请务必备份这个文件，丢失后所有加密数据无法恢复。**
2. **X 凭据** — 粘贴第一步准备的两个 Cookie。
3. **支付卡** — 输入卡信息和账单信息（卡号会自动校验）。想启用多卡轮换，向导完成后用 `xgift cards add` 追加更多卡，缺少的账单字段会自动继承。
4. **代理** — 选直连、按提示填 AnyTLS 节点，或粘贴 sing-box 配置；保存前会实际启动验证配置是否有效。
5. **Stripe 公钥** — 粘贴 `pk_live_` 公钥。
6. **商品目录** — 直接回车使用 X Premium 默认目录（3/6 个月套餐），或自定义商户、币种和套餐。
7. **站点配置** — 输入你的域名（如 `https://xp.example.com`），向导会生成 `site.env` 和随机的后台管理员密码（只显示一次，同时保存在文件里）。

完成后运行 `./bin/xgift status`，六条记录全部显示 `verified` 即为成功。

### 第四步：启动网站

把向导生成的 `site.env`、`admin-password`、`vault-password` 放到安全目录（生产建议 `/etc/xgift/`，权限 0600），然后：

```sh
sudo systemctl link $PWD/deploy/xgift.service   # 或直接复制到 /etc/systemd/system/
# 编辑 deploy/xgift.service 中的路径使其与你的安装位置一致
sudo systemctl enable --now xgift
```

`site.env` 各字段含义：

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `XGIFT_ORIGIN` | 站点完整域名（`https://` 开头） |
| `XGIFT_LISTEN` | 监听地址，只能回环，如 `127.0.0.1:8787` |
| `XGIFT_DATA_DIR` | 数据目录（vault.db、site.db 所在） |
| `XGIFT_PASSWORD_FILE` | 保管库密码文件路径 |
| `XGIFT_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE` | 后台密码文件路径 |
| `XGIFT_PAYMENTS_ENABLED` | `true` 开放充值，`false` 暂停（不消耗兑换码） |

### 第五步：配置 HTTPS 反向代理

程序只监听本机端口，需要 Caddy（或任意反向代理）提供 HTTPS。`deploy/Caddyfile` 是模板，把 `xp.example.com` 替换成你的域名后放到 Caddy 配置目录并 reload 即可。模板默认只放行 Cloudflare 回源 IP，不用 Cloudflare 时删掉 `@cloudflare` 相关段、保留 `reverse_proxy` 即可。

验证：

```sh
curl https://你的域名/healthz     # {"ok":true,...} 即成功
```

### 第六步：开始使用

浏览器打开 `https://你的域名/admin`，输入用户名 `admin` 和向导生成的密码：

1. 在「生成兑换码」选套餐、数量、批次名，点生成，复制或下载兑换码发给用户。
2. 顶部「统计概览」随时查看兑换进度和成功率。
3. 用户打开 `https://你的域名`，输入兑换码和 X 用户名即可完成充值。

## 日常维护

```sh
./bin/xgift status              # 检查所有加密记录是否完好
./bin/xgift check               # 测试代理能否访问 x.com
./bin/xgift import-chrome       # macOS：从本机 Chrome 重新导入 X Cookie（过期时用）
```

更新配置用 `put`（从标准输入读取新值）：

```sh
./bin/xgift cards list                                     # 查看卡池和当前轮换组合（只显示尾号）
echo '{"number":"...","exp_month":"05","exp_year":"2031","cvc":"123"}' | ./bin/xgift cards add
echo '新的ct0等JSON' | ./bin/xgift put --name cookies      # 还有 card / cards / proxy / api-auth
echo 'pk_live_新公钥' | ./bin/xgift put --name stripe-key
echo '{"merchant":"acct_...","currency":"bdt","plans":[...]}' | ./bin/xgift put --name catalog
```

付款卡按「卡 × 节点」组合随机轮换：每 3 个连续订单使用同一组合；任意订单被拒后立即换组合，被拒的那张卡进入 30 分钟冷却（其他卡继续轮换），补单也走同一逻辑。支付方明确 `do_not_try_again` 时该卡永久封锁直到显式解除。`cards add` 追加或更新（同卡号替换），`cards remove --last4 1234` 移除，`cards rotate` 立即结束当前组合，`cards unblock` 清除冷却与永久封锁。

## 常见问题

**密码文件丢了怎么办？** 无法恢复。加密数据全部作废，需要删除 `vault.db` 后重新运行 `xgift setup`。请把它和数据库一起备份。

**X Cookie 过期了？** macOS 上用 `./bin/xgift import-chrome` 一键刷新；其他系统重新从浏览器复制后用 `put --name cookies` 更新。

**想暂停充值？** 把 `site.env` 里 `XGIFT_PAYMENTS_ENABLED` 改为 `false` 并重启服务。用户兑换会被婉拒，兑换码不消耗。

**付款被拒怎么办？** 明确拒付会显示失败说明并阻止重复提交，不再显示自动核实。网页和 CLI 在同一个 `checkout.lock` 下执行付款，提交间隔至少 30 秒，重启仍保留间隔。付款按「卡 × 节点」组合随机轮换，每 3 个连续订单使用同一组合；普通拒付会立即结束当前组合，并**先冷却该出口节点及其共享 IP（30 分钟）**，同一张卡马上换其他节点继续付款；只有同一张卡在两个不同节点都被拒，才冷却整卡 30 分钟。其他卡继续轮换，下一次提交（含补单）自动换到新的组合，不因连续次数暂停全站。支付端明确返回 `do_not_try_again` 时只永久封锁被拒的那张卡；仅当所有卡都被永久封锁时才暂停全站，可用 `xgift cards unblock` 显式解除（同时清除冷却，不能通过补单确认框解除）。后台补单页会实时显示每张

填 POSTGRES_PASSWORD、可选 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY docker compose up -d # 拉取 autumn27/artex 镜像 + postgres # → http://localhost:8787 ``` 镜像已含常用工具（ripgrep/curl/vim/npm/nmap…）；`./skills` 与 `./data` 以绑定挂载持久化。 远程 MCP 可在系统设置中选择 `http`（Streamable HTTP）或 `sse`（旧版 SSE）。 旧版 SSE 服务通常使用 `GET /sse` 建立事件流，再通过服务返回的 `/message?sessionId=...` 接收 JSON-RPC 请求；配置时将 URL 填为 `/sse`，请求头按 `Authorization=Bearer ` 填写。 ### 方式三：下载预编译二进制（Releases） 到 [Releases](https://github.com/Hinln/ARTEX/releases) 下载对应平台的 zip，解压后得到 `artex` + `start.sh`（Windows 为 `start.bat`）+ `skills/` + `config.example.json`： ```bash cp config.example.json config.json # 填好 database 连接 ./start.sh # → http://localhost:8787 ``` > 请用 `start.sh` / `start.bat` 启动，而不是直接跑 `./artex`。它是个守护脚本：程序退出后按退出码决定是否重新拉起，**页面上的[一键更新](#方式一页面一键更新推荐)靠它完成换装**。直接运行 `./artex` 时更新完就不会被拉起了。 > 后台常驻：`nohup ./start.sh >artex.log 2>&1 &`。 ### 方式四：从源码编译单二进制 ```bash # 1) 前端静态导出 cd web && npm ci && npm run build:static && cd .. # 2) 拷进内嵌目录 cp -r web/out server/webui/dist # 3) 编译（-tags embedui 才内嵌前端） CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags embedui -o artex ./cmd/artex ./start.sh ``` ### 方式五：构建跨平台 Release 压缩包 `build.sh` 会先构建并嵌入前端，再使用 Go linker 去除调试信息，并将发布文件压缩为 zip。Release 模式默认生成 Linux amd64/arm64、macOS amd64/arm64 和 Windows amd64 的 zip 包： ```bash ./build.sh --release # 产物：dist/artex-0.3.3-*.zip ``` UPX 自解压二进制可能与部分 Linux 内核、虚拟化环境或安全策略不兼容，因此默认不启用。可用 `ARTEX_TARGETS` 自定义目标；确认目标运行环境兼容时，可显式传入 `--upx` 进一步缩小二进制： ```bash ARTEX_TARGETS=linux/amd64,windows/amd64 ./build.sh --release ./build.sh --target linux/amd64 --upx ``` --- ## 更新升级 > 升级只换程序、不动数据：Postgres 数据卷 `pgdata`、`./data`（jwt.key / SQLite 等）、`./skills` 都会保留。**数据库迁移无需手动执行**——`artex` 每次启动会幂等重跑 `schema.sql`（含 `ADD COLUMN` / `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`），即“重启即迁移”。升级前仍建议先备份 `./data` 与数据库。 ### 本仓库的私有 Release 更新源 页面一键更新固定从 [Hinln/ARTEX Releases](https://github.com/Hinln/ARTEX/releases) 检查和下载版本。克隆或通过 Git 更新源码也使用 `Hinln/ARTEX`；原项目的 Go module 路径保持不变。 这是私有仓库。请为运行 ARTEX 的后端进程设置 `ARTEX_UPDATE_GITHUB_TOKEN`，令牌只需本仓库的 **Contents: read** 权限。令牌由后端用于查询 Release 和下载附件，不发送给浏览器，也不要提交到 Git。 ```bash # 先在当前 shell 或服务环境中安全设置 ARTEX_UPDATE_GITHUB_TOKEN ./start.sh ``` 本地直接启动时，`start.sh` 不会自动读取 `.env`；必须将变量导出到进程环境。Docker Compose 部署则可在未纳入 Git 的 `.env` 中填写该变量，并重建 artex 容器；镜像需要包含本分支的更新代码，旧版镜像不会因此切换升级源。 需要先在本仓库发布非 draft、非 prerelease 的正式 Release，并附上 `artex-<版本>--.zip` 和 `SHA256SUMS`，页面才能提供可安装更新。仓库里只有源码时还不能在线升级。现有 Release 工作流会在推送 `v*` tag 时为当前仓库生成这些附件。 ### 方式一：页面一键更新（推荐） 在 **系统配置** 页（侧边栏「系统配置」→ `/system/settings`）的**版本与更新**卡片里，可以直接检查并安装新版本，无需登录服务器。 点「更新」后：下载当前平台的发布包 → 比对 Release 的 `SHA256SUMS` → 用 `-h` 冒烟测试新二进制 → 暂存为 `artex.new` → 程序退出，由 `start.sh` / `start.bat` 重新拉起并完成换装。页面会自动等到新版本上线后刷新。 - **失败不会留下坏程序**：校验或冒烟不通过就丢弃暂存件、继续跑当前版本；换装后的新版若连续 3 次启动失败，会自动回滚到 `artex.old`（失败的那个留作 `artex.failed` 供排查）。 - **随时可回退**：上一版本保留为 `artex.old`，卡片上有「回滚到上一版本」。注意数据库结构不会回退。 - **更新会中断正在运行的任务**——更新即重启，请在空闲时进行。 - **开发构建不给更新**：版本号是 `dev` 或 `git describe` 带后缀时禁用，避免正式版覆盖掉本地调试的二进制。 - **Docker 下只换程序、不换镜像**：镜像

content.readme:
Git designed for AI agents.

Anthropic built **Scion**, a faster version control system for coding agents, and described it in [Redesigning source control](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control): a server-centric system built for hundreds of agents that read, write and land code at the same time. Scion is internal to Anthropic and is not available to the public. So I built **gitai**: an open-source version of that design that anyone can run, and that the community can improve and maintain together. MIT licensed. Vendor neutral: the server never calls a language model, and every AI feature works with any provider, or none. gitai is an independent implementation of the publicly described design. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. --- ## Why Classic Git hosting was built for humans who clone a repository, work for hours and push once. Coding agents work differently: thousands of short-lived tasks, each touching a few files, each wanting to land in seconds, all on the same branches. Full clones, merge queues and client-side history walks become the bottleneck. Scion's answer is to move the work to the server: clients stay online and fetch only what they need, history questions are answered (and cached) by the server, changes land through a compare-and-swap instead of a queue, every update is an entry in a changeset log, and the repository state lives in a consistent database plus object storage so servers scale out. gitai implements these ideas, with normal Git repositories underneath. ## The Scion ideas, implemented | Scion idea | In gitai | |---|---| | **Always-online clients** that fetch exactly what they need | `ObjectService` serves single objects and sparse trees; `graft clone` and `graft sparse` materialize only the paths you ask for. | | **Source control as an API**: history runs on the server | Blame, path history, ancestry and code search run server-side and are memoized as derived data, computed once per commit. | | **Landing without a merge queue** | `UserLand` rebases a change onto the current tip and lands it with a compare-and-swap; concurrent lands on one branch are batched into a single reference update. | | **Automatic conflict resolution** | A conflicting land is resolved by a resolver you choose (any LLM provider, a deterministic tool, or none) through a versioned, vendor-neutral protocol. A model's resolution is only a proposal: it lands by itself only if the `verify.command` you configure passes on the exact tree that would land, and otherwise the agent gets the conflict package with the proposal. The deterministic rules you configure need no such condition of their own, and are verified on the exact tree as well when you turn the verification on (`verify.enabled`). | | **Changeset log** | Every accepted reference update is recorded with its operation and actor in a dense, ordered log that clients list or watch live. | | **Storage core: a database and object storage, stateless servers** | Each change is a changeset in a write-ahead log in SQLite or PostgreSQL, with a compare-and-swap per reference; packs live in object storage (file, S3, GCS, Azure). Server nodes are caches that any node can rebuild, so you add nodes to scale. | | **Test after landing, revert the culprit** | `graft-verify` tests the tip, bisects a failure and reverts the change that broke it. | | **Monitoring agents ("superfans")** | Agents follow the changeset stream and report what matters to each component, also through Slack. | | **Agent-friendly review** | Reviews with semantic approval rules: a comment-only change can need fewer approvals than a logic change. | | **Agents as first-class users** | Per-agent tokens, an RPC allowlist and branch policies decide what each agent may do. | | **Strict cache tiers** | `graft-cache` caches immutable objects in daemon and regional tiers, verifying every object. | ## Architecture ``` agents, CI jobs, sparse workspaces graft CLI / Go SDK | v gRPC +-------------------------------------------------+ | graft-cache (optional daemon and cache tiers) | +----------------

Operating-system `LANG` does not select the application language. Requests prefer `lang`, then supported `Accept-Language` preferences, then the `scopeweaver_locale` cookie, then the server default. New HTTP-created tasks retain their language across queues and restarts; older tasks without saved language use the server default. Built-in agent guidance and output instructions use the run language; user-edited templates and stored evidence remain intact. Report/CSV/ZIP labels use the export request's language. [Full documentation](docs/README.md) and [Korean references](docs/ko/README.md) include the bundled skill guidance. The presentation follows the [approval-detail component from AegisHook](https://github.com/RuoJi6/AegisHook/blob/main/web/src/components/CallDetail.vue), reusing the upstream component and theme. ## Asset sync (ScopeSentry) You can sync asset data directly from [ScopeSentry](https://github.com/Autumn-27/ScopeSentry), which saves you from collecting the same data twice: - On the **Asset sync** page, enter your ScopeSentry address and API key to connect the data source. - Choose what to sync by **project** or by **task**, and pick the asset types (domain / subdomain / IP / port / site / endpoint …). - Import in one click. Assets are merged into the company asset scope and go straight into the asset graph for agents to explore. --- ## Installation Run only one active ScopeWeaver server per PostgreSQL database. content.readme:
# UnfairPlay

UnfairPlay recovers a FairPlay model from an enrolled Mac and uses it to
decrypt personalized iOS IPAs. It is a standalone Go program.

It does not log in to Apple, buy apps, or download IPAs. You can use ipatool or
another downloader for that part.

## Legal and ethical use

Use UnfairPlay only with apps you lawfully acquired and accounts and devices
you control. It is intended for interoperability, preservation, and authorized
research. The authors do not condone piracy, credential theft, copyright
infringement, or unauthorized distribution of decrypted apps.

## Build

```sh
go build -o unfairplay ./cmd/unfairplay
```

## Usage

First, sign in to the native Mac App Store. Install an iPhone or iPad app and
open it once. Download a matching encrypted IPA with the same Apple Account.

Set up reusable decryption once:

```sh
sudo ./unfairplay setup \
  --app /Applications/App.app \
  --ipa App.ipa
```

The saved model is private. It is tied to the Mac App Store enrollment, not to
one app, so it can decrypt other personalized IPAs from the same enrollment.

Decrypt another IPA:

```sh
./unfairplay decrypt --input AnotherApp.ipa
```

The default model directory is inside the user configuration directory. Set
`UNFAIRPLAY_MODEL_DIR` or pass `--model` to use another location.

IPAs with extensions and watch apps are decrypted in one pass. Test without
keeping plaintext with:

```sh
./unfairplay verify --input AnotherApp.ipa
```

### Convert an IPA for macOS

This requires an encrypted IPA personalized for the same Store enrollment as
your saved model. Convert it with:

```sh
./unfairplay convert-ipa-macos --input App.ipa
```

The default output is `App.macos.ipa`. Use `--output` to choose another path or
`--force` to replace an existing output.

The command uses a saved version-2 enrollment model. You can instead use a
matching private 16-byte credential:

```sh
chmod 600 credential.bin
./unfairplay convert-ipa-macos \
  --input App.ipa \
  --credential credential.bin
```

The conversion:

- validates and rewrites the personalized SINF into the macOS layout;
- preserves its app key, signature, rights, and other private fields;
- adds every SINF copy declared by Apple for encrypted frameworks and
  extensions; and
- leaves all Mach-O executables byte-identical and encrypted.

The result is still an IPA, not a macOS installer. A macOS iOS-app wrapper or
compatible installer must preserve this basic layout:

```text
App iOS.app/
  WrappedBundle -> Wrapper/App.app
  Wrapper/App.app
  Wrapper/iTunesMetadata.plist
```

The converted IPA and wrapper contain a private account license. Keep them
private. This feature does not decrypt, modify, re-sign, or bypass checks inside
the app. Apps may still reject macOS, require unavailable hardware, or depend on
services that are not present on macOS.

## Advanced commands

`collect` and `recover` expose the two setup stages for diagnostics and
archived captures. `doctor` checks a capture, IPA, or model. `profile` inspects
an arm64e fairplayd without executing it.

```sh
sudo ./unfairplay collect --app /Applications/App.app --ipa App.ipa --output App.capture
./unfairplay recover --capture App.capture --output App.recovery
```

Create a code profile for an exact fairplayd binary:

```sh
./unfairplay profile --binary /path/to/fairplayd.arm64e \
  --recovery-profile-output fairplayd.recovery-profile.gz
```

The profile contains code locations and import names. It contains no account
data and does not execute fairplayd. It helps add native support for new macOS
builds, but creating it alone does not enable decryption.

## FAQ

### What is an enrollment?

An enrollment is the FairPlay state created when an Apple Account uses the Mac
App Store on a Mac. It links the account, Mac, and FairPlay selector. `setup`
turns that state into a reusable private model.

### What are SINF, SUPF, SIDB, and SC Info?

- **Personalized SINF:** an app license created for one Store enrollment. It
  identifies the enrollment and protects the app-specific key.
- **SUPF:** per-executable records used to derive keys and IVs for encrypted
  Mach-O pages. Apps, extensions, frameworks, and watch apps may each have one.
- **`SC_Info`:** the directory inside an installed app or IPA that contains its
  SINF and SUPF license files.
- **System `SC Info`:** the private Mac FairPlay state directory. Its SIDB and
  SIDS files contain enrollment state, not app content.

These files are private. Do not publish or share them.

### Do I need to run setup for every app?

No. One model can decrypt different IPAs personalized for the same enrollment.
Each app still has its own key inside its personalized SINF.

### Why might another macOS build fail?

Apple changes fairplayd code and state layouts between builds. UnfairPlay fails
closed when a path is not verified. It never publishes a recovered model until
the matching IPA decrypts and passes validation.

Patches and test reports are welcome. Include the macOS

The open-source helpdesk.

Features · How it works · Quick start · Self-hosting · Docs · Community · Support

⭐ Help more teams find opendesk. Star this repo!

## opendesk opendesk brings your support email, live chat and help center into one shared inbox, and every change shows up live for everyone on the team. It ships as a hosted service at [opendesk.sh](https://opendesk.sh) and as a self-hosted install, and **the two run the same code**. Ollie, the built-in AI, drafts, triages and answers alongside your team, with any Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible provider, including local models. ## Features - **Shared inbox** - tickets with status, priority, assignee, team, tags and SLA; notes, merge, snooze, bulk edit - **Mailboxes** - forward your support address in, reply from it through Google, Microsoft or SMTP - **Live chat** - an embeddable widget with identity verification, typing and live delivery - **Knowledge base** - collections and articles, published to a public help center - **Ollie and bots** - drafts, summaries, triage, translation and chat answers from your knowledge base - **Automations and SLAs** - rules that run on ticket events, and targets per priority - **Reports and CSAT** - volume, response and resolution times, breaches and satisfaction - **Integrations** - Linear, GitHub, Jira, Sentry, Slack, Stripe and any MCP server - **Public API** - the REST API the app itself uses, plus signed webhooks, a realtime socket and MCP - **Apps** - desktop for macOS, Windows and Linux, and a native iPhone app ## How it works opendesk is one Go binary (the API, background jobs and the event relay), an Elixir realtime gateway that holds no database connection, and Postgres. Every change that someone else should see is written as an event in the same transaction as the change; the relay publishes it to NATS, the gateway pushes it to browsers, and webhooks deliver it to your endpoints. There is no Redis and no Kafka. ```mermaid flowchart LR B["Browsers · apps"] --> C["Caddy"] C -- "/socket" --> RT["Realtime gateway"] C --> OD["opendesk
API · jobs · web app"] OD --> DB[("Postgres")] OD -- "events" --> N{{"NATS"}} N --> RT OD --> WH["Webhooks"] OD --> M["Google · Microsoft · SMTP"] ``` Self-hosted, NATS runs embedded in the opendesk binary and the whole stack sits behind Caddy on one domain. The hosted service splits the same binary into API and worker roles. Full write-up in the [introduction](https://docs.opendesk.sh/getting-started/introduction/) and the [cloud architecture](https://docs.opendesk.sh/cloud/architecture/). ## Quick start You need Go, Node.js with pnpm, Elixir, and Docker for Postgres. ```bash git clone https://github.com/useopendesk/opendesk && cd opendesk cp .env.example .env make dev-db # Postgres on localhost:55432 make api # the Go API and workers, with embedded NATS on :4222 make realtime # the Elixir gateway on :4000 make web # the web app on :5173 ``` Open `http://localhost:5173` and sign up. Until you configure a mail driver, verification and invitation emails are printed to the API log. `make site` and `make docs` run the marketing site and the docs. More in the [contributing guide](https://docs.opendesk.sh/contributing/). ## Self-hosting

# Gately

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [한국어](README.ko.md) | [Español](README.es.md) | [Français](README.fr.md) | [Deutsch](README.de.md) | [Русский](README.ru.md) | [Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md)

An open-source, auditable network gateway toolkit for home networks, NAS boxes, cloud hosts, and servers of all kinds. DDNS, STUN traversal, port forwarding, reverse proxy, certificates, WAF, and more ship in a single ~32 MB file.

> **fnOS users:** Gately ships as a native fnOS app. It plugs into the **fnOS unified gateway**, so it opens from the fnOS desktop icon and works over the same address you use for fnOS, including your remote domain, with no extra port to open. Once enabled, **fnOS administrators can sign in directly with their fnOS session**, without a Gately password or two-step code. See [fnOS native app](#fnos-native-app).

![Gately overview](docs/images/overview.webp)

![Web services: reverse proxy, static files and redirects by domain, with WAF, IP rules and sign-in per site](docs/images/web.webp)

![Per-site traffic stats: requests, errors, backend health, top client IPs and countries](docs/images/site-stats.webp)

![Port forwarding with SNI routing: one port 443 shared by several services](docs/images/portforward-sni.webp)

![Dynamic DNS](docs/images/ddns.webp)

![Intrusion protection: fail2ban-style bans synced to nftables](docs/images/guard.webp)

![Docker](docs/images/docker.webp)

![frp: several frpc and frps instances, with proxies grouped by client](docs/images/frp.webp)

![Web terminal: SSH, Telnet and the local shell in the browser](docs/images/terminal.webp)

![Configuration history with diff and one-click rollback](docs/images/config-history.webp)

![Built-in API docs](docs/images/api-docs.webp)

## Why Gately

Gately is fully open source, so users and the community can read the source and the configuration directly. For software that sits on your network edge and holds your DNS keys and certificate private keys, open source lets you see exactly what it does. Gately's commitments:

- The source is released under Apache-2.0 and open to community review
- No connections to any project-operated server by default and no device information reported; third-party sign-in uses your own OAuth apps, with no relay in between
- Every outbound address (public IP lookup, STUN servers, and so on) is visible, editable, and can be turned off
- Configuration is plain-text JSON, so you can put it under git for auditing and rollback

## Features

| Module | Capabilities |
| --- | --- |
| Dynamic DNS | Alibaba Cloud, Cloudflare, Tencent Cloud, DNSPod, Huawei Cloud, GoDaddy, Porkbun, dynv6, DuckDNS, Amazon Route 53, OVHcloud, Gandi, NS1, Bunny DNS, Namecheap, DynDNS2 (No-IP, Dynu, …), custom callbacks; IP discovery via URL, network interface, or command; IPv4/IPv6; webhooks |
| STUN traversal | TCP/UDP, keep-alive, UPnP/NAT-PMP, built-in forwarding, webhooks and scripts triggered on address change |
| Port forwarding | TCP/UDP, IPv4/IPv6, port ranges, multi-target failover, connection limits, traffic statistics, PROXY protocol v1/v2; SNI routing that lets several services share one port such as 443 (TLS passthrough by domain, a default target, PROXY protocol per route) |
| SSL certificates | Automatic ACME issuance and renewal via DNS-01 (wildcard) or HTTP-01 (no DNS provider needed), short-lived certificates and certificates for public IP addresses (Let's Encrypt shortlived profile), EAB, upload, read from file, map to a directory and run a script; after renewal, push certificates to other hosts over SSH and run a command, or restart the Docker containers that use them |
| Tailscale | Managed tailscaled (userspace networking, container-friendly) or attach to an existing system daemon; auth keys / login links, Headscale, subnet routes, exit nodes, peer list and SOCKS5 proxy, fixed port, extra tailscaled arguments and environment variables; online install, update, rollback and uninstall on Linux; restore default settings |
| frp | Multiple frpc and frps instances, each running on its own: frpc client (tcp/udp/http/https/stcp/xtcp proxies, changes apply instantly) and frps server (port allowlist, subdomains, dashboard); one-click import of legacy ini and new toml configs; online install, update, rollback and uninstall; restore default settings |
| Cloudflare Tunnel | cloudflared token tunnels and trycloudflare quick tunnels, multiple tunnels, automatic restart, public address display; online install, update, rollback and uninstall; restore default settings |
| Web services | Per-domain reverse proxy / redirect / static files / fixed text / close connection (like nginx return 444); HTTPS and HTTP/3 (QUIC); HTTP and HTTPS on the same port (redirect or serve); WebSocket; PROXY protocol in and out; basic auth, web auth, GitHub/Google/QQ/OIDC sign-in, shared users with TOTP two-step verification and single sign-on across subdomains, a built-in OIDC

Automate real Android phones from your code.
Test your apps, script the tasks you repeat, run a shelf of phones, or let an AI agent use one.
Python, Node.js, the shell or HTTP. No ADB, no USB cable, no root.

Website · Docs · Download · Sponsor · Quick start · Languages · Guides

English · 한국어 · 简体中文

No ADB, no cable
Install one app on the phone, turn on its permissions and pair it with a QR code. No developer options, no USB debugging, no root.		 The same command everywhere
touch is touch in Python, Node.js, the CLI, HTTP and as an MCP tool, all generated from one spec.		 Phones anywhere
The phone connects out to your PC, so it works on the same Wi-Fi or on mobile data through a tunnel or a relay you run. Every line is encrypted end to end.
## What people use it for * **Testing your own app** on real phones, including flows that cross into other apps, such as a login with a code from a text message. * **A shelf of phones** running the same routine every day, each through its own network or proxy. * **Giving an AI agent hands**: through MCP, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other agents can look at a phone screen and act on it. * **Small personal automations**, such as turning Wi-Fi off at night or collecting a value from an app every hour. Droidline uses only permissions an ordinary app can get, so a few things are out of reach: see [What it cannot do](#what-it-cannot-do). ## See it in action


Try the same demo in your browser, and pick elements on a simulated screen, on droidline.dev

## Quick start You need a PC (Windows, macOS or Linux) and an Android phone with Android 9 or later, on the same Wi-Fi for a first try. The [installation guide](https://droidline.dev/docs/install/) walks through each step with screenshots. 1. **Run the server on your PC.** Download the `droidline` archive for your system from [Releases](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Droidline/releases/latest), put `droidline` on your `PATH`, and start it. Leave it running. ```bash droidline serve ``` 2. **Install the app on the phone.** Download `droidline-agent.apk` from the same release page and open it. # Open Screen Sharing

![Open Screen Sharing on iPad connected to macOS and vphone-cli](assets/readme/hero.png)

Open Screen Sharing aims to develop superior servers and clients based on the private protocol used by Apple VNC (macOS's Screen Sharing server and ScreenSharing.app).

## Installation

### iOS

[![Download on the App Store](assets/readme/app-store-badge.svg)](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/open-screen-sharing/id6818992574)

The App Store version is **\$1 through October 31, 2026**, then **\$2**. Your purchase supports my work.

The App Store version excludes the following features due to App Store restrictions:

* **Apple VNC server:** relies on background keep-alive mechanisms and a lockdown exploit.
* **Dragging files directly from a remote Mac into other iOS/iPadOS apps:** relies on a private API.

To use these features, sideload the app by adding the source to SideStore or AltStore:

```
https://github.com/nekohasekai/open-screen-sharing/releases/latest/download/altstore.json
```

Or download [OpenScreenSharing.ipa](https://github.com/nekohasekai/open-screen-sharing/releases/latest/download/OpenScreenSharing.ipa) and sideload it.

### macOS

Download and install [OpenScreenSharing.pkg](https://github.com/nekohasekai/open-screen-sharing/releases/latest/download/OpenScreenSharing.pkg).

### Nightly builds

You can download and install nightly builds from the [Nightly release](https://github.com/nekohasekai/open-screen-sharing/releases/tag/nightly). For AltStore or SideStore on iOS, the source URL is:

* Fixed language switching
* Exclusive mouse support
* Debug HUD support
* Interactions optimized for iOS and iPadOS

# jactionlint **Catch broken and insecure GitHub Actions workflows before they run.** [![CI status](https://github.com/jdx/jactionlint/actions/workflows/ci.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jdx/jactionlint/actions/workflows/ci.yaml) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jdx/jactionlint?label=release&color=0f766e)](https://github.com/jdx/jactionlint/releases/latest) [![Go reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/jdx/jactionlint/v2.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jdx/jactionlint/v2) [Documentation](https://jactionlint.jdx.dev) · [Playground](https://jactionlint.jdx.dev/playground) · [Rules](https://jactionlint.jdx.dev/rules) · [Changelog](https://github.com/jdx/jactionlint/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
jactionlint is a static checker for GitHub Actions. It reads your workflows, composite actions and `dependabot.yml` and reports two kinds of problems: the mistakes that make a run fail or misbehave, and the patterns that let an outsider run code in your repository or steal its token. It started as a fork of [actionlint](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) and covers its checks, and its security rules follow the audits of [zizmor](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor). - **Correctness.** Unknown keys and events, type errors in `${{ }}` expressions, wrong inputs of actions and reusable workflows, and broken `needs:`, cron and glob patterns. [shellcheck](https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck) and [pyflakes](https://github.com/PyCQA/pyflakes) check the scripts of `run:` steps. - **Security.** Script injection, excessive token permissions, dangerous triggers such as `pull_request_target`, cache poisoning, credentials left in the checkout and AI agent actions that outsiders can steer. - **Policy.** Actions used by a tag instead of a commit, and workflows without `permissions:`, a job timeout or a concurrency group. - **Fixes.** `jactionlint --fix` repairs what has a mechanical fix, and `--diff` shows the change first. - **Gradual adoption.** Profiles choose how much is checked, and a baseline fails the build only on new findings. - **No network unless you ask.** The [online checks](https://jactionlint.jdx.dev/online), which ask GitHub about archived repositories, impostor commits and published advisories, run only with `--online`. Try it without installing anything in the [playground](https://jactionlint.jdx.dev/playground), which runs jactionlint in your browser. ## Quick start Install jactionlint with [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) and run it at the root of a repository: ```sh mise use -g jactionlint jactionlint ``` With no arguments, jactionlint checks the workflows, composite actions, `dependabot.yml` and Actions lock file of the repository. Pass file names to check only those, or `-` to read standard input. It exits with status 1 when a finding of level `error` is left. Other ways to install it: - **Homebrew:** `brew tap jdx/jactionlint https://github.com/jdx/jactionlint`, then `brew install --cask jdx/jactionlint/jactionlint`. - **PyPI:** `uvx jactionlint` runs it without installing it, and `pipx install jactionlint` or `uv tool install jactionlint` installs it. - **Docker:** the image `ghcr.io/jdx/jactionlint` also holds shellcheck and pyflakes. [Run the image](https://jactionlint.jdx.dev/ci#run-the-image) shows the command. - **Go:** `go install github.com/jdx/jactionlint/v2/cmd/jactionlint@latest`. - **Release archives:** download the archive for your platform from the [releases](https://github.com/jdx/jactionlint/releases) and [verify it](https://jactionlint.jdx.dev/install#verify-the-download). Packages named `actionlint`, as in Homebrew core, install the original project, not this fork. [Installation](https://jactionlint.jdx.dev/install) covers every method. ## Example This workflow has a typo in a trigger, untrusted input in a script and an undefined matrix property. It also uses an action by tag and sets no permissions, timeout or concurrency group. Save it as `test.yaml`: ```yaml on: push: branch: main jobs: test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - run: echo "${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}" - run: echo "${{ matrix.os }}" ``` `jactionlint test.yaml` prints each finding with its position, a message, the line it points at and, in brackets, the ID of its rule: ``` test.yaml:1:1: workflow has no "concurrency:", so every run of it executes at the same time even when a newer run supersedes the older ones. add a top-level "concurrency:" with a "group:" and "cancel-in-progress: true" [concurrency-limits] | 1 | on: | ^~~ test.yaml:3:5: unexpected key "branch" for "push" section. expected one of "branches", "branches-ignore", "paths", "paths-ignore", "tags", "tags-ignore", "types", "w

# whatnow

*Executive function for the rest of us.*

whatnow is a day planner for ADHD brains. Rather than an hourly schedule, it holds your day loosely:
what you must do, what you should do, and what you could do if there's room. Dump everything on
your plate in whatever words come out. An LLM sorts it into tasks and events, notices how you feel
about them, and plans a day that fits your energy. When you're stuck, ask it *what now?*

It runs locally: one Go binary with a web UI and a terminal UI, and your data in SQLite on your
machine. You bring your own model API key.

![Today: the day strip, tasks in must, should, and could tiers, and the chat pane](docs/screenshots/today.png)

For a feel of a whole day, from the morning brain dump to the wrap-up, read [demo.md](demo.md).

## What it does

- **Good morning:** reconcile yesterday's leftovers, dump what's on your mind, say how much you've
  got in you today, and get a plan in three tiers.
- **What now?:** one pick for right now, with a reason. Pass on it and say why, and it picks again.
- **Chat:** "push the dentist to Thursday", "break this report into tiny steps". The assistant acts
  directly, and every change can be undone.
- **Pace:** five levels, from *running on fumes* to *go hard*. Change it any time and the plan
  follows.
- **Nudges:** before events, when they end, and as the day winds down, in the web UI.
- **Wrap up:** see what you got done, triage what's left, and leave a note for tomorrow.
- **Integrations:** pull today's meetings from Google Calendar (by each calendar's secret iCal
  address, no OAuth), and pick tasks from Jira tickets (by your own JQL search) and from the PRs
  a running [Review Queue](https://github.com/oreillymedia-ai-transformation/review-queue) ranks
  for your review. Pulls happen only when you ask, from the morning brain dump or from settings.
  When hosted whatnow can't reach your Jira, because it's behind a VPN or on an intranet, set
  Jira to *From my computer* and run `whatnow jira setup` once on a Mac that can reach it (install
  with `brew install jameynakama/tap/whatnow`). After that, `whatnow jira push` sends your search
  and the next pull offers it.

You can shape it in settings. *Assistant style* sets its voice ("playful and friendly, with the
odd koan"). *About me* tells the planner how you work ("my focus peaks before lunch", "meetings
drain me"). *Theme* swaps the look: the default sticker style, plain 90s, Neon Nights, Terminal,
Paper, or Vaporwave.

## A day, in pictures

All of these come from one made-up Thursday run against a live model, with the *About me* above
set to "focus peaks before lunch, cooked after 3pm, meetings drain me".

| | |
|---|---|
| ![The morning brain dump](docs/screenshots/morning-dump.png) **Good morning:** dump it all, messy is fine. | ![The morning plan in three tiers](docs/screenshots/morning-plan.png) **The plan:** the dreaded report goes first, while focus is high. |
| ![A what-now pick with its reason](docs/screenshots/what-now.png) ***What now?*** 11 minutes before standup, so not the report. | ![Chat breaking the report into tasks](docs/screenshots/chat.png) **Chat:** break the report into steps, then add them as tasks, with undo. |
| ![Wrap-up triage of the leftovers](docs/screenshots/wrap-triage.png) **Wrap up:** each leftover comes with a suggestion. | ![The goodnight reflection](docs/screenshots/goodnight.png) **Goodnight:** a reflection that reads your note for tomorrow. |

![The six themes side by side](docs/screenshots/themes.png)

## Install

You'll need an API key for Anthropic, OpenAI, or an OpenAI-compatible provider to run it (see
[Models](#models)).

On a Mac, with [Homebrew](https://brew.sh):

```sh
brew install jameynakama/tap/whatnow
```

### Without Homebrew

Download the latest release:

```sh
curl -fLo whatnow https://github.com/jameynakama/whatnow/releases/latest/download/whatnow-darwin-arm64
chmod +x whatnow && sudo mv whatnow /usr/local/bin/
```

On an Intel Mac, swap `arm64` for `amd64`. The binary isn't signed, so downloading it through a
browser gets it blocked by Gatekeeper. `curl` doesn't, and `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine whatnow`
undoes a browser download.

### From source

You need [Go](https://go.dev/dl/) 1.27+, Node 24, and [just](https://github.com/casey/just).

```sh
git clone https://github.com/jameynakama/whatnow
cd whatnow
just install   # builds the web UI and puts whatnow in your GOBIN
```

## Models

whatnow works with Anthropic (the default) or any OpenAI-compatible API, such as OpenAI,
OpenRouter, Ollama, or LM Studio. Set it up on the first run, or later in settings. Keys are
stored in your OS keychain, never in the database. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the
environment works too.

Consumer subscriptions (Claude Pro or Max, ChatGPT plans) can't power whatnow. It needs an API key.

## Usage

```sh
whatnow          # the terminal UI, which also serves the web UI at http://127.0.0.1:7777
whatnow serve    # the web

# Chrome Relay

Lets your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Paseo, pi) use **your everyday Chrome**, with your real logins, from the command line, **in background tabs**: nothing takes focus, nothing on your screen moves. - **Whole goals in one command.** `chrome-relay do "Invite the new teammate as an admin" --data "Email=ada@example.com" --until "text:Invitation sent"` fills, clicks and checks every step, in about the time an agent spends on one click. [More](#whole-goals-in-one-command-chrome-relay-do) - **Or step by step**, with checked commands that answer in tens of milliseconds (`open`, `snapshot`, `click`, `fill`). [More](#step-by-step-chrome-relays-own-commands) - **Sign-ins without you.** Google account hops are clicked through; other logins come from the 1Password vaults you share with it (passwords, 2-step codes, passkeys), typed by Chrome Relay so the agent never sees them. [More](#signing-in-with-1password-optional) - **Approvals on your iPhone** when you're away from the Mac, with Face ID. [More](#approving-from-your-iphone) - **An audit trail** of everything every agent did. [More](#audit-trail)

**Status** - **Mac service:** built from source on your Mac ([Setup](#setup-once-per-mac-2-minutes), about 2 minutes). - **Chrome extension:** [in the Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/mdglmmedlbkjphgolcejpphnbclkfnom) (unlisted: only at that link). - **iPhone app**, Chrome Relay Approve: [on TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/zhpm8gND) (install TestFlight on the iPhone, then open the link there); in App Store review. - **Password managers:** 1Password only, for now. **The core** is background tabs with your logins, `chrome-relay do`, Google sign-in hops and an audit trail. **Everything else is optional** and off until you turn it on: 1Password, Secure Enclave passkeys, iPhone approvals, and a TypeSafe key for the fastest decider. See [What's optional](#whats-optional). Nothing installs the extension for you, and it only runs on Macs whose owner set it up. ## How it works ``` chrome-relay open/click/fill/... ──unix socket /driver──┐ chrome-relay do ──────────────────unix socket /driver───┼──▶ relay (127.0.0.1:9333, LaunchAgent) ──ws──▶ Chrome Relay extension ──chrome.debugger──▶ agent tab agent-browser (optional) ─────────ws (DevTools)─────────┘ ▲ │ └── reads the page and acts, in that agent's own tabs only └── do decides: saved flows → the agent's data → Jev or Haiku (Claude Code) → hand back to the agent ``` - **Extension** (`extension/`, MV3, one per Chrome profile you load it in): opens each agent tab **inactive** in a collapsed "Agents" tab group and runs DevTools commands in it via `chrome.debugger`. No remote-debugging port, so Chrome never shows "Allow remote debugging?". Chrome does show "Chrome Relay started debugging this browser" while agents work. - **`chrome-relay`**: one Go program, **built and signed on your own Mac** (`./build`). As a background service (`chrome-relay serve`) it is the relay: a DevTools endpoint per agent, where each agent sees and controls only the tabs it opened and commands that could raise or focus the browser are swallowed. It is also the CLI (setup, the connection URL, `do`, diagnostics, audit trail), and the optional 1Password vault and passkeys, whose Secure Enclave and Touch ID code (`internal/macos`, Swift) is linked into

# Mediarium Mediarium is a self-hosted media manager. Find a movie or show, and it searches your Usenet and torrent indexers, downloads the best release, unpacks it, names it and puts it in your library, ready for Plex, Jellyfin or Emby. It does the jobs of Radarr, Sonarr, Prowlarr, SABnzbd, a torrent client and Bazarr in **one app**: one container, one web page, one search bar, one thing to update and back up. - **Movies and TV** (anime, daily shows and specials included), plus **music**, **ebooks** and **audiobooks** if you switch them on. - **Mediarium Books**, a built-in reader and audiobook player that opens as an app of its own and remembers your place on every device. It reads Kindle books too, jumps between audiobook chapters, and follows book series. - **Tags** such as Kids or 4K, which also show up as collections in Plex, Jellyfin and Emby. - **Discover and search** everything from one place, across all your indexers. - **Built-in downloaders** for Usenet and torrents, with repair and unpacking. - **Built-in VPN** for torrents (WireGuard), with no special container permissions. - **Quality profiles** with upgrades and fallbacks, automatic searching and retries. - **Family accounts with permissions and requests**: choose what each person can do, and anyone who can't add titles sends a request for you to approve. - **Subtitles** picked to match your exact file, with a timing fix when one is out of sync. - **What's been watched**, read from Plex, Jellyfin and Emby, with watch statistics and optional cleanup rules (all off until you switch them on). - Notifications, media-server refresh (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Audiobookshelf, Kavita), download hours, backups, and your own script after each import. - **Move over from Radarr, Sonarr, Prowlarr, SABnzbd** and eight other apps without redoing your setup. They are only read, never changed. - Runs on **Synology, Unraid, QNAP, any Linux server** and 64-bit Raspberry Pi. **Privacy:** there are no ads, and Mediarium sends nothing about you or your library anywhere. It asks once whether you want to share a small anonymous message a day (a random ID, the version and rough device sizes) so the project can see which devices are popular: it is off until you say Yes, the numbers are public at [mediarium.app/stats](https://mediarium.app/stats/), and the code is open. [What exactly is sent](docs/usage-stats.md). Mediarium is new. Movies and TV work end to end, and so do music, ebooks and audiobooks once you switch them on. It's used daily, but expect some rough edges.
